author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
Same pattern as VT (#655) — the credit driving the $429 isn't the retirement credit, it's the **Utah Homeowner's/Renter's Relief** (Circuit Breaker) under Utah Code § 59-2A-205 (renter) / § 59-2A-305 (homeowner).

Per the [official Utah Tax Commission page](https://tax.utah.gov/relief/homeowner-renter-relief/):

> "To apply for renter refund, complete and submit Form TC-90CB"

And TC-90CB is a **separate form**, not part of TC-40 (income tax return). The relief is administered as a separate refund — same structural pattern as VT's renter credit, MN's renter credit, and PA's property tax / rent rebate.

For this filer (single, age 75, rent $18,363, AGI ~$33K):
- Statutorily eligible: age 65+ ✓, income below threshold ✓
- Computed amount: **$429** (per PE)
- But the credit goes on **TC-90CB, not TC-40** — so TaxAct's TC-40 doesn't show it, and TAXSIM correctly omits it from siitax

PE-US currently routes `ut_homeowner_renter_relief` through [`ut/tax/income/credits/refundable.yaml`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/ut/tax/income/credits/refundable.yaml) → `ut_income_tax` → siitax. Per the statute, that's wrong — the relief isn't on TC-40 at all.

Filed PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#8561 to remove from `ut_refundable_credits` while keeping it in [`state_property_tax_credits.yaml`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/household/state_property_tax_credits.yaml) (where it's already listed for 2025+). Will close this once that PR lands.
